findings.problem: Both theorems repeat the same long argument for differentiating a translated, scaled function. They build hinner (the fderiv of x ↦ x - x₀ is id), build houter (a const_mul of a differentiable function), compose them, apply the result to basisVec i, and finish with the same calc that turns `r ^ 2 • L ∘SL id` into `r ^ 2 * L (basisVec i)`. Lines 154-195 and 260-303 are the same proof with only the inner function changed, from heatKernel to heatKernelSpaceDerivative · τ i. The restated fderiv expressions make each proof about 45 lines.
findings.proposed_change: Add one private lemma, for example `fderiv_const_mul_comp_sub_apply`. Its statement is: for `f : Vec3 → ℝ`, `c : ℝ`, `x₀ x v : Vec3`, and `hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f (x - x₀)`, we have `(fderiv ℝ (fun y : Vec3 => c * f (y - x₀)) x) v = c * (fderiv ℝ f (x - x₀)) v`. Proof sketch: `hf.hasFDerivAt.const_mul c` composed with `(hasFDerivAt_id x).sub_const x₀`, then `.fderiv` and `simp`. In the first theorem, the change at lines 175-176 already puts the goal in the shape `fderiv (fun x => backwardHeatTestFunction r (x - x₀) _) z.1 (basisVec i)`, so after `unfold backwardHeatTestFunction` it is the lemma with `f := fun y => heatKernel y τ`, followed by `heatKernel_fderiv_apply_basisVec_local hτ i`. The second theorem is the same with `f := fun y => heatKernelSpaceDerivative y τ i`, followed by `heatKernelSpaceDerivative_fderiv_apply_basisVec hτ i`. Each use then needs only the differentiability hypothesis, which the next finding also supplies as a lemma. No new imports are needed. Both rewritten uses keep their hypotheses (ht : z.2 - t₀ < r^2, so hτ : 0 < r^2 - (z.2 - t₀)).
findings.benefit: This removes about 60 duplicated lines of chain-rule bookkeeping. A reader sees directly that the derivative of a translate is the translate of the derivative. Any later translated derivative (for example a third derivative) becomes a one-line application instead of a third copy.

findings.problem: The same differentiability argument is written out four times. It rewrites heatKernel (or heatKernelSpaceDerivative) to the explicit Gaussian formula and calls `fun_prop (disch := positivity)`. It appears at lines 78-84 and 92-101 for the generic t. It appears again at lines 161-168 (hheat) and 269-280 (hdiff) with t instantiated to `r ^ 2 - (z.2 - t₀)`, where the whole formula is retyped with that long expression.
findings.proposed_change: Add two private lemmas, `heatKernel_differentiableAt_space {x} {t} (ht : 0 < t) : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun y : Vec3 => heatKernel y t) x` and `heatKernelSpaceDerivative_differentiableAt_space (ht : 0 < t) (i) : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun y : Vec3 => heatKernelSpaceDerivative y t i) x`. Their proofs are the existing blocks at lines 78-84 and 92-101, stated once for a generic t. The two helper lemmas then use `hdiff := heatKernel_differentiableAt_space ht` and the corresponding second lemma. The two centered theorems pass `hτ`, so hheat and hdiff become one-liners. A search of the CKN directory found no existing lemma of this form.
findings.benefit: This removes four copies of the rewrite-and-`fun_prop` pattern, two of which spell out the long expression `r ^ 2 - (z.2 - t₀)` repeatedly. The formula-based differentiability proof is then maintained in one place, and the theorem proofs show only the derivative calculation.
